_comment: Public halves only. The private key lives in the CI secret HR_SIGNING_KEY and
nowhere else - not on a workstation, not in a gitignored file. An agent that
can reach the signing key can sign its own verdict, which is the arrangement
signing exists to prevent. A key derived from anything readable on the host -
a hardware id, a machine fingerprint - is a key the agent can derive too, and
cannot be rotated without replacing the host.
To activate: run hr keygen, paste the public entry below, and set
HR_SIGNING_KEY and HR_SIGNING_KEYID as repository secrets.
While this list is empty, hr validate attestation passes only because there
are no artifacts to verify. The moment one exists, it refuses.
Each entry may carry notBefore, notAfter and revokedAt as RFC3339 instants.
All three are optional; a key with none is valid for all time. They are
checked against WHEN THE ARTIFACT WAS SIGNED - taken from the ledger's
`emitted` entry, which is hash-chained and so cannot be backdated - never
against now. Revoking a key therefore refuses everything it signed after the
revocation instant while leaving the legitimate history behind it verifiable.
To rotate: add the new key with notBefore = now, set notAfter on the old key
to the same instant or later, and keep the old entry forever. Deleting it
would strand every artifact it ever signed.
To revoke a compromised key: set revokedAt to the earliest instant you
believe it was exposed, not to now. Everything it signed from that moment on
stops verifying, which is the point.
